prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The 2010 Conservative manifesto invites Britons to “join the government of Britain” under a clear creed: we are all in this together. It offers a shift from big government to the Big Society—devolving power from the centre to people, families, professionals and local communities; coupling sound money and enterprise with social responsibility; and restoring trust through openness and accountability.

Economic renewal and fiscal responsibility
- Confront Labour’s debt crisis with an emergency budget, an Office for Budget Responsibility, £6bn early waste cuts, and a credible plan to eliminate the bulk of the structural deficit over a Parliament—protecting NHS and aid.
- Stop Labour’s “jobs tax” by raising NIC thresholds; keep interest rates low; simplify and cut business taxes (corporation tax to 25p, small companies to 20p); reduce regulation; boost exports, saving and investment.
- Build a balanced, hi‑tech, green economy via R&D support, STEM focus, trade promotion, a Green Investment Bank, and superfast broadband; reform planning to favour sustainable development.
- Get Britain working with a single, payment‑by‑results Work Programme, reassessing incapacity benefit, tougher conditionality (“work for the dole”), and support for SMEs, apprenticeships and skills.
- Control immigration with an annual limit on non‑EU economic migrants, stronger student visa rules, and integration measures.

Public services and the Big Society
- Empower social enterprises, charities and public‑sector mutuals to deliver services; create a Big Society Bank; train community organisers; launch National Citizen Service for 16‑year‑olds.
- NHS: increase funding in real terms; scrap politically driven targets; expand patient choice and transparency; give GPs commissioning power; 24/7 urgent care; Cancer Drugs Fund; tougher action on infections.
- Schools: restore discipline and teaching quality (Teach First expansion, Troops to Teachers), rigorous curriculum and exams (phonics, setting, university input), technical academies, pupil premium, and more free schools/academies—especially in deprived areas.
- Families: recognise marriage and civil partnerships in the tax system; end the couple penalty; extend flexible working and shared parental leave; refocus Sure Start on early intervention; 4,200 more health visitors; curb commercialisation of childhood.
- Crime and justice: elected police commissioners, less paperwork and more patrols; tougher knife crime sentences; overhaul licensing to tackle binge drinking; payment‑by‑results rehabilitation; Border Police Force.

Clean politics and local power
- Cut MPs and ministers’ costs; recall for MPs; cap big donations; publish spending, contracts and salaries; cull quangos; open government data.
- Localism: “open‑source” planning with neighbourhood control and incentives; local referendums and vetoes on high council tax; community right to buy; elected mayors in major cities.

Environment and energy security
- Lead a low‑carbon transition: Green Deal for homes, smart grid, renewables, new nuclear (no subsidy), CCS projects, reformed Ofgem, and conservation of habitats, biodiversity and high animal welfare.

National interest abroad
- National Security Council; match defence to strategy via SDSR; renew Trident; fix procurement; strengthen the Military Covenant.
- Liberal Conservative foreign policy: pro‑NATO, close to the US, build ties with India/China, support human rights and a two‑state solution.
- Europe: positive but firm—no Euro, referendum lock on any power transfer, seek return of powers over justice and social/employment law.
- Aid: honour 0.7% by 2013, transparency and results, focus on basics and malaria, and champion trade and wealth creation.

Overall, Progressive Conservatism: sound money, enterprise, trust in people—and a Big Society where shared responsibility mends a broken politics, economy and society.
